problem.summary: 机器学习模型（如神经网络和Bag of Words模型）在图像分类任务中表现优异，但通常作为黑盒运作，缺乏对分类决策的可解释性，这限制了人类专家验证系统推理和获取额外信息的能力。

motivation.summary: 在医疗影像、机器人等关键应用中，理解分类决策的原因至关重要。现有方法无法提供像素级别的贡献解释，阻碍了人类专家对决策的验证和进一步分析。

core_idea.summary: 提出一种通用方法，通过逐层相关性传播（Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation, LRP）对非线性分类器进行像素级分解，将分类决策分解为每个输入像素的贡献，并可视化为热力图，以直观解释分类依据。

method.summary: 方法包括两个主要部分：1）针对Bag of Words特征和核分类器的分解方法；2）针对多层神经网络的逐层相关性传播。LRP通过约束传播规则（如相关性守恒）逐层反向传播输出层的相关性得分，最终分配给输入像素。此外，还讨论了基于泰勒分解的近似方法。

experiments.summary: 在多个数据集上评估：合成几何形状数据集、PASCAL VOC 2009图像、MNIST手写数字数据集以及预训练的ImageNet模型（Caffe）。实验包括像素翻转分析、不同LRP变体（如不同稳定器ε）的比较，以及与梯度方法的对比。

claims.claim: LRP能够为非线性分类器提供像素级的可解释性，生成直观的热力图。
LRP适用于多种架构，包括Bag of Words模型和神经网络，无需泰勒近似。
像素级分解结果与人类直觉一致，能够突出对分类决策重要的图像区域。
通过像素翻转实验验证了分解结果的合理性，即翻转高相关性像素会显著影响分类预测。
LRP的传播规则满足相关性守恒，确保分解的数学合理性。

limitations.limitation: 方法依赖于分类器的分层结构，对于无法分解为层的模型可能不适用。
LRP的具体实现有多种变体（如不同稳定器），选择可能影响结果。
在复杂自然图像（如ImageNet）上，分解结果可能不如简单数据集（如MNIST）直观。
未讨论计算效率和实时应用的可能性。

nodes.title: 输入图像
nodes.label: Input
nodes.summary: 原始图像像素作为输入，是分解的起点。
nodes.description: 输入图像x，其像素值x(d)是后续特征提取和分类的基础。

nodes.title: 特征提取层
nodes.label: Feature Extraction
nodes.summary: 从输入图像中提取特征，如Bag of Words特征或神经网络的隐藏层激活。
nodes.description: 对于Bag of Words模型，包括SIFT特征提取、量化和池化；对于神经网络，包括卷积、激活和池化操作。

nodes.title: 分类器层
nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.summary: 基于提取的特征进行分类决策，输出预测分数f(x)。
nodes.description: 可以是核支持向量机（SVM）或神经网络的输出层。输出f(x)是相关性传播的起点。

nodes.title: 逐层相关性传播
nodes.label: Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation
nodes.summary: 核心方法，将输出层的相关性逐层反向传播到输入像素。
nodes.description: 从输出层的相关性R(l+1)开始，通过传播规则计算每层神经元的相关性R(l)，最终得到输入像素的相关性R(d)。传播规则需满足相关性守恒等约束。

nodes.title: 像素级相关性
nodes.label: Pixel-wise Relevance
nodes.summary: 每个输入像素的相关性得分R(d)，表示其对分类决策的贡献。
nodes.description: R(d)可正可负，正表示支持分类，负表示反对。这些得分可映射到颜色空间，可视化为热力图。

nodes.title: 热力图可视化
nodes.label: Heatmap Visualization
nodes.summary: 将像素相关性可视化为热力图，供人类专家直观解释。
nodes.description: 热力图突出显示对分类决策重要的图像区域，帮助验证决策和聚焦分析。

deltas.before: 梯度方法仅提供局部敏感性，可能无法反映全局贡献，且结果可能包含噪声。
deltas.after: LRP提供全局的、像素级的贡献分解，满足相关性守恒，结果更直观。
deltas.why_it_matters: LRP生成的热力图更符合人类直觉，能够突出对分类决策真正重要的区域，而非仅对输入变化敏感的区域。

deltas.before: 现有方法可能仅适用于特定模型（如线性模型或特定神经网络）。
deltas.after: LRP被设计为通用方法，适用于Bag of Words模型和多种神经网络架构，无需泰勒近似。
deltas.why_it_matters: 通用性使得LRP可以广泛应用于不同的分类系统，提高了方法的实用性。

deltas.before: 黑盒模型缺乏可解释性，人类专家无法验证决策依据。
deltas.after: LRP提供像素级解释，允许人类专家验证决策并聚焦感兴趣区域。
deltas.why_it_matters: 在医疗影像等关键应用中，可解释性对于信任和验证至关重要。

variables.name: f(x)
variables.description: 分类器的预测输出分数

variables.name: R_d
variables.description: 输入像素x(d)的相关性得分

formulas.intuition: 分类器的输出被分解为所有输入像素的相关性之和，每个像素的贡献R_d可正可负，正表示支持分类，负表示反对。

variables.name: R_{i \leftarrow k}^{(l, l+1)}
variables.description: 从第l+1层神经元k到第l层神经元i的相关性消息

formulas.intuition: 每个神经元的相关性等于所有传入消息之和，这是LRP传播规则的核心，确保相关性在层间守恒。

variables.name: z_{ik}
variables.description: 神经元i对神经元k的加权贡献，z_{ik} = a_i w_{ik}

formulas.intuition: 相关性消息按加权贡献的比例分配，贡献越大的神经元获得越多的相关性。这是LRP的一种具体实现规则（ε规则）。

main_result.description: 在包含多边形和圆形的合成图像上，使用Bag of Words模型和LRP进行像素分解。
main_result.result: 热力图显示多边形区域获得正相关性，圆形区域获得负相关性，背景区域接近零，与分类器决策一致。

main_result.description: 在真实图像上使用Bag of Words模型和LRP进行像素分解。
main_result.result: 热力图突出了目标物体的关键部分，如人脸的眼睛和嘴巴，验证了方法的有效性。

main_result.description: 在MNIST上使用神经网络和LRP进行像素分解，并进行像素翻转实验。
main_result.result: 热力图显示数字的关键笔画区域获得高相关性；像素翻转实验表明翻转高相关性像素会显著降低分类置信度。

main_result.description: 使用Caffe的预训练ImageNet模型和LRP进行像素分解。
main_result.result: 热力图在复杂自然图像上也能提供合理的解释，如突出物体的头部和关键特征。

ablation.description: 比较不同稳定器ε值（如ε=0.01和ε=100）和不同传播规则（如α=+2, β=-1）的效果。
ablation.result: 小ε值产生更精细的粒度和更多负相关性；大ε值使结果更平滑，负相关性减少。α和β的选择影响正负相关性的比例。

robustness.description: 系统性地翻转具有高正相关性、高负相关性或接近零相关性的像素，观察分类预测的变化。
robustness.result: 翻转高正相关性像素会显著降低真实类别的预测分数；翻转高负相关性像素会增加真实类别的预测分数；翻转中性像素影响较小。这验证了分解结果的合理性。

scaling.description: 从简单合成数据到复杂自然图像（ImageNet）的评估。
scaling.result: 方法在简单数据集上解释非常直观；在复杂图像上也能提供合理解释，但可能不如简单数据集清晰。

case_study.description: 分析数字'4'和'9'的像素分解，解释分类器如何区分它们。
case_study.result: 对于'4'，顶部空白区域获得正相关性；对于'9'，同一区域获得负相关性，因为'9'需要顶部闭合。这展示了方法揭示分类器决策细节的能力。

terms.definition: 逐层相关性传播，一种将分类器输出分解为输入像素贡献的方法，通过逐层反向传播相关性得分实现。
像素级分解，将分类决策分解为每个输入像素的贡献，结果可可视化为热力图。
相关性守恒，LRP的一个关键约束，要求相关性在层间和节点间守恒，即总相关性从输出层到输入层保持不变。
词袋特征，一种图像表示方法，将图像表示为局部特征（如SIFT）的直方图。
基于核的分类器，如支持向量机（SVM），使用核函数计算样本相似性。
热力图，将像素相关性得分映射到颜色空间（如红-蓝）的可视化表示，用于直观解释分类决策。
稳定器，在LRP传播规则中添加的小常数，用于防止分母为零，并影响分解的粒度和负相关性的数量。

metadata.title: On Pixel-Wise Explanations for Non-Linear Classifier Decisions by Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Understanding and interpreting classification decisions of automated image classification systems is of high value in many applications, as it allows to verify the reasoning of the system and provides additional information to the human expert. Although machine learning methods are solving very successfully a plethora of tasks, they have in most cases the disadvantage of acting as a black box, not providing any information about what made them arrive at a particular decision. This work proposes a general solution to the problem of understanding classification decisions by pixel-wise decomposition of nonlinear classifiers. We introduce a methodology that allows to visualize the contributions of single pixels to predictions for kernel-based classifiers over Bag of Words features and for multilayered neural networks. These pixel contributions can be visualized as heatmaps and are provided to a human expert who can intuitively not only verify the validity of the classification decision, but also focus further analysis on regions of potential interest. We evaluate our method for classifiers trained on PASCAL VOC 2009 images, synthetic image data containing geometric shapes, the MNIST handwritten digits data set and for the pre-trained ImageNet model available as part of the Caffe open source package.

Abstract

Understanding and interpreting classification decisions of automated image classification systems is of high value in many applications, as it allows to verify the reasoning of the sys- tem and provides additional information to the human expert. Although machine learning methods are solving very successfully a plethora of tasks, they have in most cases the dis- advantage of acting as a black box, not providing any information about what made them arrive at a particular decision. This work proposes a general solution to the problem of understanding classification decisions by pixel-wise decomposition of nonlinear classifiers.
We introduce a methodology that allows to visualize the contributions of single pixels to pre-

dictions for kernel-based classifiers over Bag of Words features and for multilayered neural networks. These pixel contributions can be visualized as heatmaps and are provided to a human expert who can intuitively not only verify the validity of the classification decision, but also focus further analysis on regions of potential interest. We evaluate our method for clas- sifiers trained on PASCAL VOC 2009 images, synthetic image data containing geometric shapes, the MNIST handwritten digits data set and for the pre-trained ImageNet model available as part of the Caffe open source package.

Finally, it can be seen from the formulas established in this section that layer-wise relevance propagation is different from a Taylor series or partial derivatives. Unlike Taylor series, it does not require a second point other than the input image. Layer-wise application of the Taylor series can be interpreted as a generic way to achieve an approximate version of layer-wise rele- vance propagation. Nonlinear learning machines are ubiquitous in modern problem solving. While highly success- ful in e.g. hard classification, regression or ranking problems, their non-linearity so far has pre- vented these models to additionally explain and thus contribute to a better understanding about the nature of the solved problem. We have introduced a tool set for deconstructing a nonlinear decision and thus fostering transparency for the user. In particular we have introduced the general concept of decomposition of a nonlinear image classification decision in terms of pixels. In other words, for a well-classified image, a heatmap can be produced that highlights pixels that are responsible for the predicted class membership. Note that this is possible without need of segmented training images. We consider heatmap- ping as an important part of the interpretation of nonlinear learning machines and its applica- bility goes far beyond what has been exemplarily presented in this work: it ranges from the interpretation of bio-medical images to the practical validation of a trained models for image classification. was applied iteratively from the output back to the input, thus, forming another possible pixel-

wise decomposition. This inherits the favorable scaling properties of backpropagation. Notably, these two methods were not defined as a particular solution to the heatmapping problem, but instead as a set of constraints that the heatmapping procedure must fulfill in order to be admissible. For instance, the exact choice of Taylor reference point was not speci- fied beyond the constraints that it should be a root and that it should be located close to the actual data point. Similarly, the layer-wise relevance propagation has been defined with the sole restriction that the propagation rule conserves class relevance on a layer and node basis. Thus, the further specification of relevance propagation rule is deferred to the appreciation of the user, or as a future work, and may either be model-specific, problem-specific, or subject to a particular practical or computational requirement. dients, or more structured visual features such as edges, corners, contours, or object parts. An important aspect of the proposed heatmapping procedure lies in the fact that it does not require to modify the learning algorithm, or to learn an additional model for heatmapping. Instead, it can be directly and transparently applied to any (pre-)trained Bag of Words model or neural network when applicable. This desirable property is demonstrated in this paper by the heatmapping of images classified by the third-party GPU-trained ImageNet neural net- work. In particular, our heatmapping procedure was applied to this network without any fur- ther training or retraining. Thus, heatmaps for the ImageNet network could be quickly produced using a modest CPU. While we have proposed in this paper several instances of pixel-wise decomposition and demonstrated their excellent performance in practice, the set of possible relevance propagation methods, and their mathematical properties, will certainly have to be further explored. A first aspect that needs to be investigated is the greediness of the layer-wise relevance propagation procedure, in the sense that it is computed one layer at a time, and its potential impact on the quality of heatmaps: While computationally advantageous, some of the backpropagated rele- vance might encounter a dead-end in the lower layers and be distributed randomly. Another open question relates to the heuristic nature of the proposed instances of relevance propaga- tion, in particular, whether the distributed relevance messages being proportional to the weighted neuron activations can be analytically justified. Finally, it is not clear how to evaluate the quality of a heatmap beyond simple visual assess- ment. In t...
discriminate between two heatmapping methods that may otherwise look of similar quality to

the human. Finding quantitative properties that are desirable for these heatmaps, or further constraints on the heatmapping procedure is therefore of nature to complement the human assessment. Future work will need to explore the many domain- and data-specific degrees of freedom in the heatmapping process in order to ultimately propose a universal metric for quantification. It is our firm belief, that heatmapping will be an important ingredient of future knowledge discovery and exploratory analysis and understanding of complex data in the sci- ences and industry, even beyond the presented field of image analysis.
